title: Equivariant conjugate product and its integral generic graph closure
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and put $K=k(S)$. Let $J$ be a finite group acting on $S$ and $k$ compatibly, with action $h_j$ on $S$. Let $u:B\to S$ be a finite $k$-morphism, with $B$ integral projective of finite type over $k$, and suppose its generic fibre is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}M$ for a finite extension $M/K$. Write $\eta_B:\operatorname{Spec}M\to B$ for the resulting generic-point map. Suppose $J$ acts on $B$ by $a_j$, semilinearly for the given action on $k$, and on $M$ by field automorphisms $\sigma_j$, with
$$u a_j=h_j u,\qquad a_j\eta_B=\eta_B d_j,\qquad d_j=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma_j^{-1}).$$
Let $r:T\to S$ be a proper $k$-morphism with $T$ integral of finite type over $k$. Suppose $T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a finite field extension $L/K$, and fix a $K$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow M$. There exist an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ and a proper surjective $k$-morphism $\pi:Y\to T$ which is an isomorphism over a nonempty open of $T$, such that, putting $v=r\pi$, one has $Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}L$ with the identification induced by $\pi$, and the following assertions hold. Write $f:\operatorname{Spec}M\to Y$ for the induced generic morphism. For $j\in J$, let $Y_j$ be the same abstract scheme $Y$ with map $h_jv:Y_j\to S$ and the induced $k$-structure. Define
$$P=B\times_S\prod_{j\in J}Y_j,\qquad q:\operatorname{Spec}M\longrightarrow P,\qquad q_B=\eta_B,\quad q_j=f d_{j^{-1}}.$$
Then these are well-defined fibre-product data, and $P$ admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $k$. There is an action of $J$ on $P$ which is semilinear on $k$ and lies over $h_g$ on $S$, specified on its projections by
$$p_B g_P=a_g p_B,\qquad p_{gj}g_P=p_j\quad(g,j\in J).$$
The map $q$ is equivariant for the action $d$ on $\operatorname{Spec}M$. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow P$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closure of the point $q(*)$. Then $C$ is integral projective of finite type over $k$, the action restricts to $C$, and $p=u p_B i:C\to S$ is equivariant. Moreover
$$C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}M,\qquad k(C)=M,$$
with the isomorphisms induced by $q$ and compatible with the actions. The projection $c=p_1i:C\to Y$ satisfies $vc=p$. The composite $\pi c:C\to T$ satisfies $r\pi c=p$. No action on $T$ or $Y$ is assumed and these projections need not be equivariant.

Field, integral scheme, finite type, function field, finite extension, finite morphism, fibre product, projectivity, closed immersion, and closure with its reduced induced structure use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-closed-immersion], and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Actions may be nonfaithful; semilinear means compatibility with the indicated automorphism of $k$. Properness, surjectivity and open immersion use [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Agent conjugate-product and generic-graph expansion of X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161; Segre: constructions.tex Tag 01WD lemma-segre-embedding; reduced closure: schemes.tex Tag 01J3 lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme. Projective birational input: coherent.tex Tag 0201 remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3), followed by properness of the immersion into projective space.

proof.text: By projectivity of $S$, its structure morphism is proper. Hence $T\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper. Apply the integral Chow theorem to $T$: obtain an integral finite-type $Y$, a proper surjection $\pi:Y\to T$, an immersion $e:Y\to\mathbf P^n_k$, and a nonempty open $U\subset T$ over which $\pi$ is an isomorphism. The composite $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper. Since $\mathbf P^n_k$ is separated over $k$, proper-over-separated makes $e$ proper; a proper immersion is closed. Thus $Y$ is projective, with exactly the birational and surjectivity assertions required.

source.place: Tags 0200 lemma-chow-Noetherian and 0201 remark-chow-Noetherian; morphisms.tex Tags 01W6 lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed and 01WC lemma-locally-projective-proper; schemes.tex Tag 01IQ lemma-immersion-when-closed

proof.text: The given nonempty generic fibre makes $r$ dominant. Its unique point maps to the generic point of $T$: the generic point of integral $T$ maps to that of $S$, and $T_K$ has just one point. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ factors through $U$, so base-changing the isomorphism $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ gives $Y_K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$. This is the identification induced by $\pi$, not a newly chosen embedding. For clarity on residue fields, on an affine chart over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, passage to the generic fibre inverts $A\setminus\{0\}$; at its generic point this leaves the fraction field unchanged. Thus the generic stalk is precisely $L$. Compose the given $K$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow M$ with this generic-fibre map to obtain $f:\operatorname{Spec}M\to Y$, and put $v=r\pi$.

source.place: Affine fibre-product localization, and morphisms.tex Tag 01RW definition-function-field; application of the dense-open isomorphism supplied by Chow

proof.text: Write $s_M=u\eta_B=vf$. The hypotheses imply $s_Md_j=h_js_M$. Therefore $h_jvf d_{j^{-1}}=h_js_Md_{j^{-1}}=s_M$, so the displayed $q_B,q_j$ have the same map to $S$. The fibre-product universal property constructs $q$. Let $b_j$ be the induced scheme automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so that the structure map of $Y_j$ is $\rho_Sh_jv=b_j\rho_Y$, where $\rho_S,\rho_Y$ are the structure maps of $S$ and $Y$. Let $e:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ be the closed immersion over $k$ of step 1, and $\rho:\mathbf P^n_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structural projection. Since $\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, the induced morphism $\varphi_j=b_j\times\mathrm{id}$ of fibre products is an automorphism of $\mathbf P^n_k$, with inverse $b_j^{-1}\times\mathrm{id}$, and satisfies $\rho\varphi_j=b_j\rho$. An isomorphism is a closed immersion, so $e_j=\varphi_je:Y_j\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ is a closed immersion with $\rho e_j=b_j\rho e=b_j\rho_Y$, the structure map of $Y_j$. Thus every $Y_j$ is projective over $k$, embedded in $\mathbf P^n_k$ with the same $n$.

source.place: Section 01JO section-fibre-products (induced morphisms of fibre products); twisted factors in the agent expansion of ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4

proof.text: Set $Q=\prod_{j\in J,S}Y_j$. The group is nonempty, and $S$ is separated over $k$ since it is proper. Apply the projective-fibre-product closed-model theorem to $Q$, using the equal-dimensional embeddings from step 3. It gives a closed immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$. Now $P=B\times_SQ\to B\times_kQ$ is a closed immersion because $S/k$ is separated. Taking the product of the chosen closed embeddings of $B$ and $Q$ gives a closed immersion $B\times_kQ\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_k\times_k\mathbf P^N_k$: each factor is a base change of a closed immersion, followed by composition. Composing with the Segre embedding gives the asserted finite-dimensional projective embedding of $P$.

source.place: Tag 01WD lemma-segre-embedding; schemes.tex Tag 01KR lemma-fibre-product-after-map; morphisms.tex Tags 01QR and 01QS

proof.text: For $g\in J$, prescribe the $B$-component $a_gp_B$ and the component to the factor indexed by $j$ as $p_{g^{-1}j}$, regarded as a morphism of the underlying schemes $Y$. Its structural map to $S$ is $h_jvp_{g^{-1}j}=h_g(h_{g^{-1}j}vp_{g^{-1}j})=h_gup_B$, also the structural map of $a_gp_B$. Thus these components define $g_P$. Comparing projections gives $(g_P)(l_P)=(gl)_P$, since the $j$-component is $p_{l^{-1}g^{-1}j}=p_{(gl)^{-1}j}$, and the $B$-component is $a_ga_lp_B$. The identity element gives the identity; hence $g_P$ is invertible with inverse $(g^{-1})_P$. Its structure map is $h_g$ composed with that of $P$, so the action is semilinear over $k$. This is precisely $p_{gj}g_P=p_j$.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property; explicit permutation calculation for ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4

proof.text: The field action gives $d_gd_l=d_{gl}$. On the $B$-projection, $g_Pq$ and $qd_g$ agree by $a_g\eta_B=\eta_Bd_g$. On the $j$-projection they agree because $p_jg_Pq=f d_{(g^{-1}j)^{-1}}=f d_{j^{-1}g}=f d_{j^{-1}}d_g=p_jqd_g$. Thus $q$ is equivariant. In particular its image point $x=q(*)$ is fixed by every $g_P$, so its closed topological closure is invariant.

source.place: Fibre-product uniqueness and the explicit inverse-index calculation

proof.text: Take the reduced induced closed subscheme $i:C\hookrightarrow P$ of $\overline{\{x\}}$. It is reduced and its underlying space is nonempty and irreducible, so it is integral. Its composite closed embedding into the projective space of step 4 makes it projective and of finite type over $k$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}M$ and $C$ are reduced, the maps $q$ and $g_Pi$ factor through $i$: their topological images lie in its support. Denote the latter factorizations by $g_C$. Factorizations through a closed immersion are unique, since on affine charts a map annihilating an ideal has a unique factorization through its quotient. Thus $g_C l_C=(gl)_C$ and $1_C=\mathrm{id}_C$ follow after composition with $i$; they form an action by automorphisms. Finally $p g_C=u p_Bg_Pi=u a_gp_Bi=h_gp$, proving the claimed equivariance and semilinearity on $C$.

source.place: Tag 01J3 lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme and Tag 0356 lemma-map-into-reduction; projective closed immersion and its properness

proof.text: We compute the generic fibre scheme-theoretically. The projection $P\to B$ is proper by proper-over-separated: $P/k$ is proper by its projective embedding and $B/k$ is separated by projectivity. Base change along $B_K=\operatorname{Spec}M\to B$ identifies its source with $P_K$, by associativity of fibre products. The induced $q_K:\operatorname{Spec}M\to P_K$ is a section of this separated projection, since its $B_K$-component is the identity. Hence $q_K$ is a closed immersion. In particular its image is a single closed point with residue field exactly $M$, without any separability assumption on $M/K$.

source.place: Tag 01KT lemma-section-immersion; morphisms.tex Tag 01W6 lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed and Tag 01W4 lemma-base-change-proper

proof.text: To compare this image with $C_K$, choose an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ and an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P$ over it. If the chart contains $x$, the reduced-closure ideal is $I=\ker(R\to M)$: the closure of the prime corresponding to $x$ is $V(I)$ and $I$ is prime. Put $W=A\setminus\{0\}$. Every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $M$, and $W^{-1}I=\ker(W^{-1}R\to M)$: a fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator does. The closed immersion in step 8 makes $W^{-1}R\to M$ surjective, hence $W^{-1}(R/I)=M$. A chart not containing $x$ misses its closure (every nonempty open of that irreducible closure contains its generic point $x$); there both closed subschemes are empty. These chart identifications agree, being induced by the same map $q$. Thus the factorization of $q$ induces $\operatorname{Spec}M\simeq C_K$.

source.place: Tag 01J3 lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, affine radical ideal description; affine localization of the generic fibre

proof.text: On a chart containing $x$, $R/I$ is a subring of $M$ and the preceding localization equals $M$. Consequently its fraction field is $M$: every element of $M$ is already a fraction with denominator in $W$, and every nonzero element of $R/I$ is invertible in $M$. The integral-affine function-field theorem identifies this fraction field with the generic stalk $k(C)$. All identifications are induced by $q$, so the equality $g_Pq=qd_g$ already proved induces the prescribed actions on both $C_K$ and its function field. In particular the pullback action on functions is $\sigma_g^{-1}$, as required by $d_g=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma_g^{-1})$.

source.place: Tag 01RW definition-function-field and Tag 01RV lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; affine fraction-field identification

proof.text: For the identity element $1\in J$ the structural map of $Y_1$ is $v$. Therefore the fibre-product relation gives $vc=u p_Bi=p$. Composing with $v=r\pi$ gives $r\pi c=p$. These projections exist as $k$-morphisms. No action on $Y$ or $T$ was used, and no equivariance for these two projections is asserted.
